content:
Here’s a list of 100 distinct statements a depressed and anxious client might say to their psychiatrist in a single therapy session. For context, imagine the client is Maya, a 34-year-old project manager who moved from Chicago to Boston a year ago, recently ended a five-year relationship, and is juggling remote work stress, caring from afar for her dad with Parkinson’s in Illinois, and the grief of losing her mom three years ago. She’s first-generation Filipino American, was raised Catholic, struggles with perfectionism and imposter syndrome, and has been having panic episodes on crowded trains. She lives alone with her rescue dog, Olive, and has been trying to get back into painting but feels stuck.

1) I woke up at 4:12 a.m. again and couldn’t get back to sleep—my brain just won’t shut up about the presentation next week.
2) Ever since the breakup with Daniel, I keep replaying every argument and wondering what I missed.
3) I feel like a terrible daughter because I’m not in Illinois helping my dad more.
4) Sundays are the worst; I get this heavy dread around 3 p.m. like I’ve already failed the week.
5) I know it’s irrational, but every time my manager Slacks me “Do you have a minute?” I’m sure I’m getting fired.
6) The stairs to the subway make my heart race because I’m scared I’ll panic underground again.
7) I tried that breathing app you suggested, but it made me more aware of how shallow my breath is and I freaked out.
8) I’ve been clenching my jaw so hard at night that I cracked a molar—my dentist mentioned a night guard.
9) I skipped breakfast all week because food makes me nauseous in the mornings.
10) I keep forgetting simple words during meetings and then spiraling about early-onset dementia, which I know is dramatic.
11) I wrote down my automatic thoughts like we discussed, and most of them boil down to “You’re not enough.”
12) I can’t concentrate on a single page of a book anymore; my mind just drifts to worst-case scenarios.
13) I miss my mom most when I smell laundry detergent—she used that Tide with the blue cap—and then I cry in the aisle at Target.
14) I googled “how to stop feeling empty” at 2 a.m. and that felt pathetic.
15) The sertraline eased the edge, but I feel kind of flat—like life is on low volume.
16) I’m drinking more coffee to wake up and then I’m jittery by 10 a.m., which probably isn’t helping.
17) I told my brother I needed help with Dad’s paperwork, and he said, “You’re the organized one,” which made me furious and guilty.
18) I skipped my friend’s birthday because the idea of small talk made me want to hide.
19) I’ve been doomscrolling before bed and then wondering why I can’t sleep.
20) I promised myself I’d paint on Saturday, but I just stared at the blank canvas and cleaned the kitchen instead.
21) It feels like there’s a knot under my sternum all day.
22) I don’t trust good days because I’m waiting for something bad to happen.
23) I’m scared you’ll think I’m being dramatic or wasting your time.
24) I recognized a cognitive distortion at work—mind reading—and still believed it anyway.
25) I bought groceries and then let the spinach rot because I didn’t cook all week.
26) When my calendar is empty, I feel lonely; when it’s full, I feel trapped.
27) I keep imagining running into Daniel on Newbury Street and not knowing what to say.
28) I can’t tell if this tiredness is depression or if I’m just lazy.
29) I replay the moment I told my mom I was moving to Boston and how she smiled but looked worried; I can’t shake that look.
30) My prayers feel more like bargaining now than comfort.
31) I feel like I’m meeting deadlines by sheer panic-fueled sprints and then crashing.
32) I tried journaling in the mornings, but it turned into a to-do list I avoided.
33) I canceled on my aunt twice because I couldn’t face family questions about marriage and kids.
34) Sometimes I think, “What’s the point?” and then I feel scared that I’m thinking that.
35) I’m not planning to hurt myself, but I do think about disappearing when things feel heavy.
36) Olive seems to sense when I’m spiraling—she nudges me—and then I feel guilty that my dog is my emotional support system.
37) I hate that I need reassurance constantly; it makes me feel needy and annoying.
38) I don’t even know what I like anymore outside of work.
39) I tried that progressive muscle relaxation and noticed my shoulders are practically glued to my ears.
40) I’m afraid of disappointing you by not getting better faster.
41) I keep seeing the number 3:12 on clocks, which is when my mom passed, and it rattles me.
42) I avoid looking at my bank app because I’m scared of what I’ll see.
43) I haven’t done laundry in two weeks, and I’m wearing a swimsuit bottom as underwear—this feels like a low point.
44) I told HR I’m “fine” during our wellness check, and I’m not sure if I was lying to them or to myself.
45) When my phone rings with an Illinois area code, I brace for bad news.
46) I worry I’m too old to start over, but too young to settle.
47) I bought a day pass to a coworking space to feel less isolated, then sat in the corner with my headphones and avoided eye contact.
48) I tried to challenge the thought “I’m failing at life” with evidence, and all I could think was “Everyone else seems ahead.”
49) The last dream I remember was me trying to climb an escalator going down while carrying my mom’s photo.
50) I don’t trust my own memory about the breakup—some days he was loving; other days he felt absent, and I minimize the absent days.
51) I started picking at my cuticles again until they bled during a meeting.
52) My appetite swings from nothing to eating cereal out of the box at midnight.
53) I keep wondering if this is just grief that never finished.
54) I felt a tiny moment of joy when I saw tulips by the Charles, and then I immediately told myself not to get used to it.
55) I zone out in conversations and then panic that I missed something crucial.
56) I’m embarrassed that a crowded Trader Joe’s can send me into a tailspin.
57) I keep telling myself I’ll try dating apps again, and then I stare at the blank bio and close it.
58) I want to feel proud of anything, even if it’s small, and I can’t access that feeling.
59) I’m scared medication will change my personality, but I also don’t want to feel like this.
60) The phrase “just relax” makes me want to scream.
61) I felt angry at my mom for dying and then immediately ashamed for feeling that.
62) I realize I talk to myself in second person: “You’re messing this up again.”
63) I tried a gratitude list and it felt fake, but I did list Olive, hot showers, and pho.
64) I avoid mirrors because I look tired and puffy, and it reminds me of how I feel inside.
65) I’ve noticed I say “sorry” for everything, even when someone bumps into me.
66) I’m not sure what I want our goals to be; part of me is scared to name them.
67) I want help with the panic on the T specifically; that’s where I lose control.
68) If a friend canceled on me as often as I cancel on myself, I’d stop trusting them.
69) I’m mad that grief isn’t linear, even though you keep saying it isn’t.
70) I keep thinking I should be “over it” by now—over the breakup, over my mom, over the move.
71) I wonder if I have ADHD because I start five tasks and finish none.
72) The silence in my apartment at night is so loud it hums.
73) When I email at 11 p.m., people think I’m dedicated, but really I’m avoiding my thoughts.
74) I felt a pang of envy when my friend announced her engagement, and then I avoided her post for days.
75) I noticed the thought “No one really knows me,” and I’m not sure I’ve let anyone try.
76) I hate how performative I feel at work, like I’m acting as a competent adult.
77) If I take a sick day for mental health, I feel like a fraud.
78) I caught myself catastrophizing again when the train stopped between stations and my heart pounded in my throat.
79) I’m worried about relying on you too much; I don’t want to be a burden here either.
80) I miss singing at church but feel like I don’t belong there anymore.
81) I’m scared I’ll never feel genuinely excited about anything again.
82) I told myself I’d run for ten minutes and ended up walking Olive around the block, which I guess is something.
83) I feel stuck between wanting to be invisible and wanting to be seen.
84) I overanalyze texts until I hate my phone.
85) I bought a plane ticket to visit Dad and then couldn’t press “confirm” for twenty minutes.
86) I want to believe rest is productive, but I only feel relief when I’m doing.
87) The thought that keeps looping is “If I slow down, the sadness will catch me.”
88) I’m curious about EMDR because these memories feel like they’re stuck on repeat.
89) I’m not sure what my values are anymore; they used to be family and stability, and now everything feels shaky.
90) I avoided drinking last week and noticed my sleep was slightly better.
91) I don’t know how to ask for help without feeling weak.
92) I’m always waiting for permission to take up space.
93) I keep checking my pulse when I’m anxious, which probably makes it worse.
94) I think I’m grieving the future I thought I’d have at 34—married, maybe a kid, closer to family.
95) A coworker praised my report, and I immediately thought they were being polite.
96) I’m tired of living like my brain is a hostile witness.
97) I don’t want to scare you, but sometimes I wish I could just sleep for a long time and not think for a while.
98) I catch myself holding my breath when I read emails.
99) I’m afraid that if I let myself cry, I won’t stop.
100) What would “better” even look like for me, realistically, and how do we get there without me falling apart on the way?
